::: {.table-scroll}
| Market state | Rule (set by the benchmark's returns) | n months | Threshold |
|:--|:--|--:|:--|
| Normal | Benchmark monthly return strictly between its 10th and 90th percentiles | 178 | −5.88% … 6.26% |
| Strong rally | Benchmark monthly return at or above its 90th percentile | 23 | ≥ 6.26% |
| Recovery | Benchmark drawdown below −5% at the previous month-end, drawdown narrowing and benchmark return positive this month | 50 | −5% drawdown |
| Downside | Benchmark monthly return at or below its 10th percentile | 23 | ≤ −5.88% |
| Tail | Benchmark monthly return at or below its 5th percentile | 12† | ≤ −7.86% |
:::

† n below 15: a small sample, descriptive only. ‡ Score clipped at 0 or 1 (4 of the 16 scores in this view): compare the raw values. § Set or bounded by the state definition: the benchmark defines the states, so on these rows its beta is 1, its returns are at or below a negative cut-off and no month is positive; read them as reference points, not as a contest. The example strategy is long–short; the benchmark is long-only.

95% intervals treat months as independent and are descriptive: t-intervals for means and for betas (OLS standard error), Clopper–Pearson intervals for hit frequencies. Overlapping states and the selection of the configuration are not accounted for. A wide interval means the history cannot pin the value down. Rows in italics are the all-months reference values, against which the state-conditional values can be read.

States can overlap: every tail month is a downside month, and 20 strong-rally months are also recovery months. Percentiles use all 224 benchmark months (a retrospective classification, not an ex-ante trading signal). Data: archived backtest (not actual trading, not audited), monthly, Apr 2007 – Nov 2025; this table is generated by the site's data pipeline at build time.
